stem: When teaching signs of post-transplant bacterial infection, which wound-related finding aligns with standard references?

options.text: Wound dehiscence never indicates possible infection
Only fever above 104°F can accompany wound complications
Wound dehiscence is a normal expected finding that requires no evaluation

explanation.rationale_correct: Signs of bacterial infection include wound dehiscence along with wound erythema, purulent drainage, tenderness, and swelling.

rationale_incorrect.B: Wound dehiscence is listed among bacterial-infection signs requiring evaluation.
rationale_incorrect.C: Fever is usually ≥101°F (38.5°C), and wound dehiscence may occur with or without high fever.
rationale_incorrect.D: Wound dehiscence warrants clinical evaluation rather than being dismissed as always benign.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 13, Post-Transplant Complications → bacterial infection → Signs and symptoms → v.

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 13 → bacterial infection → f.v. (wound dehiscence among infection signs); PDF p. 734 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Wound-dehiscence sign angle distinct from catheter-site erythema item (cctc-3139) and drainage/output changes (cctc-3135); anchor verified on Cupples p. 734.

stem: A febrile transplant recipient with purulent JP drain output is being evaluated for bacterial infection. Which diagnostic step aligns with standard references?

options.text: Obtain cultures of the wound, throat, urine, sputum, JP drainage, and/or stool as indicated
Cultures are never indicated when drainage is present
Only blood cultures are obtained and JP drainage is never cultured
Empiric antibiotics should be withheld until all cultures are finalized in two weeks

explanation.rationale_correct: Bacterial infection diagnosis includes cultures of the wound, throat, urine, sputum, JP drainage, and/or stool as clinically indicated, along with blood cultures and imaging when appropriate.

rationale_incorrect.B: Drainage and wound sources are among indicated culture sites.
rationale_incorrect.C: JP drainage may be cultured in addition to blood and other sources rather than being excluded.
rationale_incorrect.D: Empiric antibiotics are administered after cultures are obtained rather than being withheld for weeks.

stem: After bacterial infection cultures return with organism identification, which treatment principle aligns with standard references?

options.text: Adjust antibiotic treatment based on the sensitivities of the identified bacteria
Continue empiric broad-spectrum therapy indefinitely without review
Discontinue all antibiotics once any culture is positive
Sensitivity results are never used to guide transplant infection therapy

explanation.rationale_correct: After empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics are started, antibiotic treatment is adjusted based on the sensitivities of the identified bacteria.

rationale_incorrect.B: Therapy is tailored to culture and sensitivity results rather than continuing empiric therapy indefinitely without adjustment.
rationale_incorrect.C: Targeted therapy follows identification and sensitivities rather than stopping all antibiotics solely because a culture is positive.
rationale_incorrect.D: Sensitivity-guided adjustment is specifically described in bacterial-infection management.

stem: A coordinator is updating bacterial-infection treatment protocols. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Antibiotic treatment should be adjusted based on the sensitivities of identified bacteria.
Immunosuppression may be decreased with caution during severe bacterial infection.
The patient should be observed for symptoms of rejection during infection treatment.

explanation.rationale_correct: Sensitivity-guided antibiotics, cautious immunosuppression reduction, and rejection monitoring are supported during bacterial infection treatment. Statement IV is false because wound infections are treated with appropriate antibiotics based on culture and sensitivities.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement III is also true—patients should be observed for rejection symptoms during infection treatment.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement IV is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement IV is false because wound infections receive appropriate antibiotics determined through culture and sensitivities.
